newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares finish shade higher, sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares finish shade higher, sluggish trade.

text.p: Bombay blue-chips posted small gains in sluggish trade on Tuesday as squaring up by operators at close pushed up prices, dealers said.
"Overall, there is no specific buying interest in the market," said a dealer at a domestic brokerage firm.
"The last day of settlement at the NSE brought some upward movement in share prices." Traders said scattered buying by punters to square up long positions helped pivotals end higher.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange closed 20.33 points or 0.66 percent up at a provisional close of 3,119.67. The day's high was 3,133.54.
Traders said market activity was focussed on ITC, SBI, Bajaj Auto, MTNL, Hind Lever and Glaxo.
"Foreign funds were select bidders in some counters, but mostly stayed away from the market," the dealer added.
Analysts expect the upcoming monetary policy to drive down interest rates and buoy share prices.
They said the Reserve Bank of India is expected to announce one percent cut in the cash reserve requirements of banks.
The central bank will meet on Saturday to release the monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March).
Housing finance company HDFC gained 14.25 to 2,175.25 after the company announced a 43 percent rise in 1996/97 (April-March) net profit to 1.09 billion rupees.
Ranbaxy Laboratories was unchanged at 612.25 rupees after the firm said its 1996/97 net rose 21 percent to 718 million.

TISCO rose 0.75 rupees to 171.75, SBI 1.0 to 211.0, Hind Lever 12.70 to 797.50, MTNL 3.50 to 217.50, Bajaj Auto 13.0 to 940.25 and Tata Power 3.25 to 119.25. But, ACC lost 10.50 to 1,669.50, TELCO 0.75 to 421.0 and ITC 6.25 to 310.25.
